Krynica-Zdroj Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Krynica-Zdrój, Poland

Not demolished. Jews first settled in the spa town of Krynica-Zdrój at the end of the 18th century, with intensified migration following Poland's partitions. This cemetery, established in the mid-19th century, includes an ohel with a compartment for kvitelach (petitionary prayer notes) in the Hasidic tradition. Nazi occupation brought mass executions directly at the cemetery; postwar neglect turned it into a garbage dump, and 1980s Communist authorities even considered demolishing it to build a sanatorium, though the plan never proceeded. Late-20th-century renovations restored the site with fencing and a stone wall; visitors can now request a key at the town hall.
